content.text: I couldn't open any files, so this diagnosis comes from the file list and from how this NestJS boilerplate is usually laid out. The line numbers are estimates.

candidates.explanation: The strategy that verifies access tokens on protected routes most likely has a wrong secretOrKey, for example the refresh secret or an undefined config key. It may also have a faulty validate check, such as checking a payload field that doesn't exist or isn't set when the token is issued. Either way, every freshly issued access token fails verification and gets a 401. Login and refresh don't go through this strategy, so they still work.

The access token may be signed with the wrong secret or expiry, for example the refresh secret or a zero or negative expiresIn. It may also be signed with a payload that doesn't match what JwtStrategy expects, such as 'userId' instead of 'id'. Refresh still works because it uses a separate token and strategy.

The secret or expiry env mappings could be swapped or misnamed, for example secret reading AUTH_REFRESH_SECRET or expires reading the wrong variable. That would make the access token invalid or already expired when it is used.

fix.description: Make secretOrKey use configService.getOrThrow('auth.secret', { infer: true }), the same secret AuthService uses to sign access tokens. Make validate reject only when payload.id is missing, and return the payload. Also check that getTokensData signs the access token with auth.secret and auth.expires.

It may also have a faulty validate check, such as checking a payload field that doesn't exist or isn't set when the token is issued. Either way, every freshly issued access token fails verification and gets a 401. Login and refresh don't go through this strategy, so they still work.

The access token may be signed with the wrong secret or expiry, for example the refresh secret or a zero or negative expiresIn. It may also be signed with a payload that doesn't match what JwtStrategy expects, such as 'userId' instead of 'id'. Refresh still works because it uses a separate token and strategy.

The secret or expiry env mappings could be swapped or misnamed, for example secret reading AUTH_REFRESH_SECRET or expires reading the wrong variable. That would make the access token invalid or already expired when it is used.

fix.description: Make secretOrKey use configService.getOrThrow('auth.secret', { infer: true }), the same secret AuthService uses to sign access tokens. Make validate reject only when payload.id is missing, and return the payload. Also check that getTokensData signs the access token with auth.secret and auth.expires.
